content: ISBT 128 is a globally standardized system designed for the identification, labeling, and processing of human blood, tissue, and cellular therapy products. The acronym ISBT stands for the International Society of Blood Transfusion, while 128 refers to the barcode symbology known as Code 128, which is utilized in this system. The current version of the ISBT 128 Standard Technical Specification is version 3.0.0. The first version, version 1, was introduced in 1994. It was developed to replace the older ABC Codabar and other similar CODABAR-based standards that were previously used in transfusion medicine. These older systems were less secure and carried less information. The ISBT 128 system was created with the collaboration of several organizations, including the American Association of Blood Banks (AABB), the American Red Cross (ARC), the Department of Defense, and the Health Industry Manufacturers Association. Together, they worked on developing a more advanced barcode symbology, which was eventually adopted as an international standard. To oversee the implementation and management of this new standard, the International Council for Commonality in Blood Banking Automation (ICCBBA) was established. The AABB later mandated that all AABB-accredited blood banks must fully implement ISBT 128 by May 1, 2008. The ISBT 128 system enhances standardization in transfusion medicine by assigning a unique donation identification number to each blood product. This number includes a collection facility code, ensuring that every product can be specifically identified and tracked globally. The system also standardizes the labeling of specific products and blood treatment processes, ensuring consistency across all applications. The ISBT 128 barcode is highly efficient, as it allows a significant amount of information to be encoded in a compact space. It also includes an internal check digit to prevent errors caused by barcode misreads. Each ISBT 128 barcode contains two data identifier characters that specify the type of information encoded (e.g., ABO/Rh blood group, product code). The label is divided into four quadrants for clarity. The upper left quadrant contains the donor identification number (unit number). The upper right quadrant displays the ABO/Rh blood group. The lower left quadrant includes the product code, while the lower right quadrant shows the expiration date and time (down to the hour and minute), along with any special testing information, such as antigen typing or cytomegalovirus (CMV) status.
